text:
sam: Heads-up — saw a big perf regression in nightly canary for models with nonstandard head dims (eg head_dim=48). p99 token latency jumped ~3x after the kernel selection change. Looks like FlashAttention fails to load for these shapes and we fall back to Triton slowpath a lot.

maya: I saw that too on canary-2. Repro locally with mixtral-8b-ish config. Quick numbers: baseline hosted (Flash) ~1.5k tokens/s @ batch=8, seq=1024. Canary fell to ~520 tokens/s and fallback logs show a lot of SDPA/Triton handoffs.

sam: Repro command I used:
```
rdx profile --model mixtral-8b --batch 8 --seq 1024 --head-dim 48 --runs 10
```
Logs include: `kernel_selector: candidate=flashattention compat=false head_dim=48 reason=unaligned` then `route: fallback=triton_slowpath`.

alex: That's the classic headstride/warp mismatch. Flash requires head_dim%16==0 (or %8 on new kernels). For 48 (3*16) it's weird — should be allowed for some kernels but our kernel capability matrix probably misreported. Also check RoPE scaling path because some kernels assume a particular q,k layout.

maya: Quick grep from the runtime capability table: `flash_kernel.max_unaligned = false` and `prefer_sdpa_if_unaligned = true` was added in the last rollout (deploy 1759910000). I think the rollout toggled off the new permissive flash path for performance portability.

terra-bot: Deploy 1759910000 rolled to canary-2 at 2025-11-15T03:20Z by infra/rollout-bot.

sam: Two actionable items: 1) figure out why 48 isn't matching the permissive flash kernel; 2) reduce fallback ratio by either padding heads at compile time or routing model variants to SDPA. Padding might break RoPE scaling though.

alex: Suggest route heuristic: if head_dim %8 != 0 -> route to sdpa; else allow flash. But that would route 48->flash (since 48%8==0). So problem must be deeper: maybe we check head_bytes % 128 for warp alignment (48*8=384 bits -> not multiple of 128?). We should log the exact capability check.

maya: Found the exact codepath — capability check uses `head_dim * sizeof(float16)` and then tests `(% 256 == 0)` which is wrong; should be 128 for the new GPU arch. Patch attached in gist:
```
- if ((head_dim * elem_bytes) % 256 == 0) compat = true;
+ if ((head_dim * elem_bytes) % 128 == 0) compat = true; // account for 16-byte warp lanes on Ampere/GB200
```

sam: Nice catch. Any idea about KV prefetch behavior? I noticed cache miss spikes when fallback happens, and p99 is worse than expected.

maya: Prefetch bug: when we fallback to triton_slowpath we still use the flash-prefetch offset calculator. The offset math assumes contiguous KV layout used by Flash and ends up reading wrong pages for triton buffers -> extra device->host copies. Sample log: `kvcache: prefetch_offset=384B -> mapped_ptr=null -> doing host_mirror copy`. That explains additional 30-40ms per token in worst case.

alex: So two fixes: correct capability modulus (low-risk) and decouple prefetch offset calc by kernel backend. Quick canary config to force SDPA for mixtral-8b variants while we patch.

maya: I pushed a canary rollout toggling `routing.table['mixtral-8b'].prefer='sdpa'` to canary-2. Patch:
```
routes:
  mixtral-8b:
    prefer: sdpa
    fallback_order: [sdpa, flash, triton]
```

sam: Can you run the same rd-run after that canary? I want p50/p99 numbers.

alex: Ran quick microbenchmark on canary-2 post-toggle: batch=8 seq=1024 head_dim=48 -> tokens/s = 1300 (p50), 990 (p99). Much closer to baseline. Fallback rate dropped from 65% to 7%. KV host copies reduced by ~80%.

maya: Created ticket INF-4123 to: 1) fix modulus check in kernel capability (PR #8124), 2) split prefetch offsets per backend, 3) add unit test for head_dim=48 and head_dim=56 combos.

sam: Awesome. Priorities: merge PR, run full perf regression on nightly, then remove sdpa forced route. Assigning: alex (PR + perf), maya (kvcache offset + tests). I'll link INF-4123 to the incident doc.

alex: I'll open PR today and add perf microbench script to CI.

maya: I'll add the offset decoupling and tests, plan to have a draft by EOD.

sam: Thanks team. Quick note — add a telemetry flag to record `kernel_reason` for routed requests so we can chart fallback trends over the next week. :eyes: "
